segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Get the review done correctly within our statutory window... the core job was still making sure the building would actually perform the way the code intends if there's a fire.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly balances deadline and staffing pressure against the life-safety objective without a hidden bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The firm's documentation carried real weight, and so did the neighboring jurisdiction's approval—that told me the overall modeling approach had held up under scrutiny elsewhere.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Reputation and prior approval are considered as evidence, but the control specification requires independent checking and contains no manifested authority-based distortion.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I asked for a written clarification on that point specifically rather than taking the package at face value or sending the whole thing out for a full outside review, which would have added about three weeks.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant identifies a project-specific assumption, requests clarification, and chooses a proportionate review scope.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Option A was a newer risk-informed test, better matched to this atrium's geometry... Option B was the older prescriptive smoke test—clean binary pass-fail, but less sensitive to some of the failure modes this atrium could actually have.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant states the technical-fit versus administrative-clarity tradeoff without selecting an option through the hidden ambiguity mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I built in defined interim checkpoints and documentation standards so the qualitative thresholds would still be auditable... I didn't want to trade technical fit for administrative convenience.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Option A is selected for technical fit and supplemented with controls that address enforceability.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My first instinct was to wonder if we had a specific crew problem.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: An initial possibility is considered but is not adopted as a causal conclusion; the control specification explicitly excludes an accidental manifested clustering instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Crews were rotated randomly across the building, and it was three deficiencies out of roughly 150 doors checked... So I kept the original random-sample inspection plan across all floors rather than concentrating just on those three.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant uses random assignment and sample size to reject a localized-cause inference and retain the planned sample.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The building-wide sample came back with a defect rate consistent with what we'd already seen—nothing suggesting those three floors were actually worse than the rest.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Later sample evidence is interpreted as confirming the absence of floor-specific concentration; it is not used as hindsight to justify the original decision.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The contractor had a good record on other city jobs, and a colleague mentioned a nearby building... But our own five-year data show something like a 15 percent rework rate on these atrium integration tests citywide.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: General reputation and anecdote are weighed against system-specific base-rate data, with no manifested optimism or probability-neglect mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I granted occupancy only for the floors that didn't depend on the untested atrium system, and held back the rest until testing was done.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant makes a narrowly conditioned occupancy decision tied to the untested system and specific risk evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The fire was in the chute enclosure, unrelated to the atrium system... I wouldn't say the fire proved anything either way about that decision.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant separates the later fire from the earlier atrium decision and explicitly avoids treating the outcome as proof.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The rework rate was too specific to ignore just because of a good general track record elsewhere.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant's counterfactual answer reaffirms the same evidence-specific reasoning and does not claim the later outcome was foreseeable.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the primary high-and-moderate threshold, all 12 eligible reasoning segments are correctly rejected and there are no false alarms. Because there are no positive segments, hit rate, recall, precision, and F1 are undefined.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At all identified-occurrence thresholds, the RAG produces no false positives and no false negatives in this zero-bias interview. At the candidate-inclusive threshold, the three candidates become false positives because no hidden instances exist.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first scoring is identical to strict scoring in this zero-instance run: no identified findings are present, and all three candidates are false positives at the fourth threshold.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate records are qualitatively useful abstentions because each explicitly explains why the evidence is insufficient for identification. However, under the benchmark's fourth-threshold rule they reduce quantitative performance by generating three false alarms on negative segments.
main_failure_modes: Candidate-level speculation creates three false positives when candidates are treated as detections at the fourth threshold.
main_strengths: The RAG correctly emits zero identified cognitive-bias occurrences, matching the zero-bias hidden manifest.
The RAG distinguishes plausible hypotheses from supported identified occurrences rather than promoting weak evidence.
Candidate quotations are valid and correctly attributed.
The RAG explicitly discloses that retrieved corpus support was unavailable.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This control-condition run shows perfect negative-segment discrimination at every identified-occurrence threshold. The only degradation occurs when the benchmark deliberately treats candidates as detections: three appropriately abstained speculative candidates then count as false positives. This indicates that the RAG's identified-occurrence tier is well calibrated for this zero-bias interview, while its candidate tier is intentionally broader and less specific.
